extracted.intended_audience: Mathematical Reviews / MathSciNet reviewers (mathematicians asked to write reviews)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for preparing and submitting reviews to Mathematical Reviews/MathSciNet, including TeX formatting, MSC classification suggestions, reference and remarks conventions, and post-submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS account and Reviewer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have an AMS log in Account with your Mathematical Reviews/MathSciNet Reviewer Number in the Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not set up an AMS Account, go to www.ams.org. If you have an AMS Account but did not add your Reviewer Number, add it from within your AMS Profile. After log in you are taken to 'View Reviewer Information' where you can choose items to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the item to review / entering an MR number
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an item from the list of review items on the View Reviewer Information page; click 'Review' next to the item to go to the Web Review Submission page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the item is not on the list, fill in the MR Number in the 'Enter an MR Number' box. If not on the list, put a comment in the Remarks portion (for example if the item was passed to you by a colleague).

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: At the top of the Web Review Submission form select the type of TeX to be used in processing your review (TeX, AMS-TeX, LaTeX, AMS-LaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS-LaTeX (recommended) is the default and suitable for most reviewers (over 95%). Use AMS-TeX or AMS-LaTeX if you need AMS math/symbol fonts. If your review contains only roman text (no math), formatting features of TeX are not needed and any type may be chosen. Scientific Word/Workplace output can be viewed as AMS-LaTeX—prepare as Portable LaTeX and use 'Upload Review Text'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare review text using TeX/LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: All review text should be prepared using some version of TeX/LaTeX (plain TeX, AMS-TeX, LaTeX or AMS-LaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only prose without mathematical notation, you may compose in a text application but must copy-and-paste the review text into the 'Review text' box. Do not upload PDF or Word files; these cannot be used. It is recommended to use AMS-LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use user-defined macros or external packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use your own LaTeX definitions (\def or \newcommand) or LaTeX macros; do not use \input, \usepackage, or \include commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All definitions/macros will have to be removed during editing; this can introduce errors and delay publication. External packages cannot be used in review text and including these commands may prevent creating a PDF preview. The replacement of user-defined macros with their expansions during editing can lead to errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading or pasting review text
rubrics_metrics.description: You may upload a LaTeX file via 'Upload Review Text', or copy-and-paste the review text into the review box; if pasting, select only the review text proper (leave out preamble and postamble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the wrong file is uploaded you may upload a new file which replaces the old one. Typing directly into the review box is allowed but not recommended. The text application file cannot be uploaded—copy/paste only.

rubrics_metrics.name: No graphic images; limited diagram support
rubrics_metrics.description: No graphic images can be part of a review in MathSciNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only supported diagramming package in MathSciNet is the CD package of AMS-TeX and AMS-LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: You are asked to suggest 5-digit MSC primary and optional secondary classifications for the item being reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor recommendations appear at top of submission page; not required to enter data but encouraged to recommend a unique primary classification and optional secondary ones. Enter classifications without internal spaces (e.g., '11D45'). Separate multiple secondary classifications with a space. If you agree with editor suggestions you need not fill these boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: References in review text must be complete and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: If including references, provide as much information as possible (full author name, year, journal/book/video title, title of cited item, volume and paging, MR Number if there is one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are checked for accuracy and formatted to MR style during editing. For references found in MathSciNet, copy the bibliographic data beginning with the MR Number and paste into the review text surrounded by square brackets, [...]. Though MR Number by itself is in principle sufficient, in practice it provides little or no basis for checking accuracy—include full details where possible. Using MRef (AMS service) can help find properly formatted references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Remarks box
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Remarks box to add comments for the editors that are helpful as they edit your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the Remarks box for material intended to be part of the published review. Use it for errors in bibliographic information or title translation, or to indicate intentions if preview is not as expected. Do not use it for comments about other reviews or for regular correspondence (send regular correspondence by email to [email protected]). If you submit an amended review on a later day, place a note in Remarks indicating the amended review is intended to replace the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX comments and special characters handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of special LaTeX characters: '%' starts a comment, '#' and '&' have special meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commented out material is assumed not part of the review text—better to remove commented material. If a percent character is actually needed in text use \%. If you need '#' or '&' in text use '\#' and '\&' respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and PDF preview
rubrics_metrics.description: After clicking 'Submit' you will receive a confirmation screen and the LaTeX processor will be applied to your review text; a link to view a PDF preview will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission free of LaTeX errors will produce the most satisfactory PDF preview. Recommendations: if you have access to a LaTeX processor locally, process your review locally first to ensure it's free of errors; if you need AMS fonts select AMS-TeX or AMS-LaTeX. Inclusion of external macro packages not in standard distributions is not allowed—their commands will be ignored and macros invoked from such packages will have to be removed during editing, possibly causing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making changes after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may edit your review after submitting by selecting 'Edit Review' from the confirming screen and resubmitting as many times as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you amend the review on the same U.S. Eastern day, the new review overwrites the old one. If you amend on a later day, place a note in the Remarks box indicating the amended review should replace the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lists included with MathSciNet full items
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected journals covered in MathSciNet have reference lists from individual papers included with the MathSciNet Full Item information; these are keyed and processed independently of review text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reference lists supplement but do not replace references you may add in your review text; no action is needed on your part to include these lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated confirmation of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of your review is confirmed by an automated email system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated confirmations are sent out once per day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating reviewer information and subject interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'View My Reviewer Info' to check and update your list of classes and interests, which determine items editors send you for review; you may also update name, email, or postal address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes do not take effect instantly; requests are sent to Mathematical Reviews for manual database updating. Keep postal address current, especially if away from usual location, because some items (particularly monographs) are sent in paper form.
